subject: Observability export wiring for private VPC onboarding
messages:
From: Alice Foster <alice.foster@acmehealth.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: acme-health-sre@acmehealth.com
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Observability export options for private VPC deployment

Hi Diego,

Thanks for taking this on. We're getting close to the on-prem/VPC handoff window and our security team has a few hard requirements we need to validate before we move to the final readiness review:

- Preferred delivery: Splunk HEC (mutual TLS) or local syslog forwarder only; no direct outbound to external SaaS from customer subnet unless via NAT/egress proxy.
- Tracing: we want span-level correlation back to user requests for a 30s window; prefer an OTEL collector inside the VPC that forwards to our Splunk APM ingestion.
- Retention/audit: logs must be kept in our Splunk for 365 days for specific audit indexes; we'll need example mapping of Redwoods' log fields to our SIEM fields.
- Evidence: SOC2 team asked for a sample evidence bundle (config snippets, network ports, cert thumbprints).

Can you confirm whether Redwood's private package supports HEC with mTLS and whether we can run an OTEL collector as part of the private deployment? Also please indicate normal ports outbound (HEC: 8088 or 443?), any required inbound ports for health checks, and whether there's a recommended forwarder pattern for fully air-gapped customers.

I've attached the Acme evidence template to help structure the artifact pack.

Cheers,
Alice Foster\Security Engineering\Acme Health

Attachments: acme-evidence-template.xlsx

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Alice Foster <alice.foster@acmehealth.com>
Cc: acme-health-sre@acmehealth.com
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability export options for private VPC deployment

Alice — thanks, this is helpful. Short answers up front:

- Splunk HEC with mutual TLS: supported. We can ship a config bundle that uses mTLS to a customer-controlled HEC endpoint. We support both 8088 and 443 depending on the customer's proxy rules; 443 is common when egress is limited to TLS.
- OTEL collector: supported as a deployable sidecar/daemon in the private package. We provide an example otel-collector config and a small wrapper to manage credentials.
- Inbound health checks: by default the private deployment exposes a management port on 127.0.0.1 for local health checks; external inbound isn't required unless you opt into our remote diagnostics channel.
- Air-gapped pattern: recommended is a local forwarder (customer-managed) that pulls evidence bundles on a scheduled basis; we can provide an evidence export CLI to create a signed bundle.

Next steps I propose:
1) Quick 30-min sync with your SRE and our observability engineer to align mapping and TLS cert exchange (I can host).
2) We'll produce a 'wiring checklist' (I attached a first-draft redwood-vpc-obsv-checklist.md) showing ports, sample HEC config, OTEL settings, and the evidence pack layout.
3) Marissa from our integrations team will provide Splunk HEC sample config and an OTEL collector snippet for your SIEM ingestion.

Can you do 11:00am PT today for the sync? If not, propose two slots.

—Diego
Diego Fernandez\Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference\d: +1 415-555-0124

Attachments: redwood-vpc-obsv-checklist.md

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Observability export options for private VPC deployment

Marissa / Kim — forwarding the request from Acme (below). High level asks:

- Confirm Splunk HEC mTLS workflow and provide a minimal splunk-hec-sample.conf that we can hand to the customer.
- Provide an OTEL collector config (otel-collector-config.yaml) that: 1) receives traces and metrics locally, 2) attaches Redwood span attributes for correlation (request_id, model_id, route), and 3) forwards to customer Splunk APM.
- Provide recommended ports and NAT/eproxy notes (they're likely to force outbound only via 443 through a proxy).
- A small canary plan for validating mapping to the customer's SIEM: what test events to send, sample logs that demonstrate field mapping, and a checklist for retention verification.

Notes to include in artifacts:
- Field mapping table (redwood field -> recommended Splunk index/field)
- Evidence bundle layout (config, cert thumbprint, export manifest)
- Fallback path: if HEC is blocked, fall back to a local syslog forwarder (rsyslog/Fluentd) that writes to a customer internal collector.

Forwarding the original message here for context.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Observability export options for private VPC deployment

Diego / Kim — thanks for the ping. I've sketched a pragmatic minimal delivery we can hand to Acme today and a slightly more robust pattern for their audit run. Main points below; attaching the sample configs.

Minimal (fast path)
- HEC with mTLS over 443 (recommended if outbound allowed only to TLS).
- Splunk HEC config: use token-restricted endpoint plus mTLS client cert; sample file: splunk-hec-sample.conf (attached).
- OTEL collector: run as daemonset/sidecar inside the private package; basic pipeline: receivers: otlp; processors: batch, attributes (attach request_id, model_id); exporters: splunk_hec. See otel-collector-config.yaml (attached).
- Ports: outbound 443 to <HEC_ENDPOINT>, outbound DNS/ntp as usual. No inbound open ports required for logs/traces unless you want remote debug.
- Evidence pack: include config snippets, cert thumbprint, generated manifest.json (we'll create this), and a signed bundle.

Robust (audit-ready)
- Add local forwarder pattern: Fluentd/rsyslog writes to an internal customer collector; forwarder signs and batches exports so no live outbound required.
- Add a small verification suite: 10 synthetic traces, 20 log events across error/info levels, and one large tokenized sample to confirm field extraction.

Canary / validation plan
1) Exchange test certs (mTLS) in a staging HEC endpoint.
2) Deploy OTEL collector with sampling=1.0 for synthetic traces and sampling=0.05 for production traffic.
3) Send 10 synthetic traces with identifiable request_id tags and verify in Splunk index:redwood_audit.
4) Verify retention policy: run search and confirm 365d retention on the specified index.

Deliverables I will attach to the customer: splunk-hec-sample.conf, otel-collector-config.yaml, and a short runbook checklist. I'll also sketch the manifest format for the evidence bundle so it matches their acme-evidence-template.xlsx.

I can join the 11:00am PT sync — sending invite now.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole\Integrations Lead, Redwood Inference\marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachments: splunk-hec-sample.conf; otel-collector-config.yaml
